Where it began

Prabath Jayasuriya was born in Matale on 5 November 1991. He went to Christ Church College in the town, and later Lumbini College in Colombo, and played for his school and the Matale district side as a boy.

Colombo Cricket Club gave him his senior start, with a one-day debut in December 2011 and a first-class debut in February 2012. Through the following decade he became one of the most dependable spinners in Sri Lankan domestic cricket, and in March 2021 he helped Sinhalese Sports Club win the national T20 tournament, their first title in it since 2005.

The player

He played his first one-day international in 2018, but the Test call took much longer. It finally came, at short notice, for the final Test against Australia in July 2022. He took 6 for 118 in the first innings and 12 for 177 in the match, the best figures by any Sri Lankan on Test debut, and was named player of the match.

He kept going. In the series against Pakistan that followed, he took five wickets in each of his first three Test innings, joining Tom Richardson and Clarrie Grimmett as the only bowlers to do so. In April 2023 he took 7 for 52 against Ireland, his best, and reached 50 Test wickets in only seven matches, quicker than any spinner before him.

By November 2026 he had played 25 Tests from 2022 to 2026 and taken 134 wickets at 32.00, with 12 five-wicket innings and two ten-wicket matches.

What made him special

He bowls left-arm orthodox spin, and Galle proved especially kind to him: seven of his first eight five-wicket innings came there. Against New Zealand he took 6 for 42 as they were bowled out for 88, their lowest total against Sri Lanka, and was player of the series. No Sri Lankan bowler got to 50 Test wickets at home faster, and none got to 100 faster either.

His batting has been described, generously and fairly, as that of a lower-order man who can bat a bit. By November 2026 his best Test score was 28 not out, and as any tailender will tell you, the not out is the important part.

Away from the middle

Honours followed the wickets. He was the ICC's Player of the Month for July 2022, his very first month in Test cricket, and Sri Lanka Cricket named him its best Test bowler of 2025. In the Lanka Premier League he played for the Jaffna Stallions.

And finally

Few cricketers have needed less time to settle into Test cricket, after waiting so long to be asked. He seems to have spent the wait working out exactly where to land the ball.
